subject: Storage horizon primer — concrete examples for requests vs. results
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@summitcare.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@summitcare.com
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot question — what exactly do you keep by default?

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Legal asked for a short, concrete summary we can give compliance — specifically: for the hosted pilot, please list with examples what Redwood keeps by default and for how long. They're asking for simple categories we can paste into our vendor questionnaire.

Example they want: 
- "User request (raw text) — kept? for how long?"
- "Model-generated answer — kept? for how long?"
- "Intermediate streamed fragments / k/v cache — kept?"

Can you provide a one-page equivalent (examples + timelines) and any pointers on how customers can opt-out or request erasure?

Appreciate it,
Emma Liu
Procurement, SummitCare
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@summitcare.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot question — what exactly do you keep by default?

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear examples. Below is a concise primer you can paste into the questionnaire. I attached a short matrix (redwood-retention-matrix.pdf) and a sample erasure log for evidence.

Summary (default hosted behavior unless customer-configured otherwise):

1) Customer request / input (prompts, user messages)
- Example: "What are the nearest dialysis centers to 94107?"
- Default: Stored for 45 days by default for telemetry and quality monitoring.
- Why: short window helps with debugging, model quality checks, and billing reconciliations.
- Opt-out: Customers can enable immediate non-persistence (no-store) at account or route level; also supported via conversation flags in the API.

2) Model-generated answers (final completions / responses)
- Example: The LLM's returned text or structured JSON output.
- Default: Stored for 90 days by default (longer than raw requests because we track outputs for regression monitoring and evals).
- Opt-out: Can be disabled for specific routes; note disabling also removes ability to use Redwood Optimize features that rely on output sampling.

3) Streamed fragments and KV cache snapshots
- Example: partial tokens sent via streaming, KV cache content used to accelerate autoregressive decoding.
- Default: Ephemeral; live streaming buffers and KV caches persist for the duration of the session and are purged immediately after the session closes (<= 24 hours in edge cases). They are not written to long-term storage by default.

4) Audit logs / usage metadata (latency, token counts, error traces)
- Example: request_id, latency_ms, token_count per request.
- Default: Retained for 365 days for operational analytics and SLA investigations. Pseudonymized where possible.

5) Attachments and runtime artifacts (files uploaded to the request)
- Example: invoice.pdf uploaded as context.
- Default: Stored under the same retention policy as the request unless the customer marks the upload as ephemeral. Sensitive file types can be configured to auto-delete on session end.

Deletion and evidence:
- On customer erasure request: We remove customer-identifying raw inputs and outputs from accessible stores within 72 hours and schedule background job to delete backed-up snapshots; proof-of-deletion artifacts (timestamped job entries) are available — see sample-erasure-log.txt attached.
- For compliance audits we can produce an export showing deletion job IDs and timestamps (we do not include underlying binary attachments in the export — only metadata).

Exceptions / notes:
- Aggregated telemetry used for model improvement is aggregated and de-identified; it is not reversible to user inputs.
- Legal holds: If a customer requires a data hold, retention can be extended per contract and will be tracked in Redwood's compliance ledger.

Next steps: If you want, Kimberly can run a one-paragraph version tailored to SummitCare's vendor questionnaire.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Security & Compliance Liaison
Redwood Inference
From: security@summitcare.com <security@summitcare.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Liu <emma.liu@summitcare.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot question — what exactly do you keep by default?

Olga,

Thanks for the breakdown — very helpful. Two follow-ups from our security team: 

1) Prompts that contain PHI/PII — are those retained under the request bucket and subject to the 45-day window? If we flag a conversation as containing PHI at ingestion, can you automatically shorten retention to immediate purge?

2) Can you provide a short example of the deletion evidence we get back? We need to confirm it contains a deletion-job-id, affected-record-ids, and timestamps.

Also, does the 90-day outputs window include derived embeddings or are embeddings treated separately?

Thanks,
Julian Perez
InfoSec, SummitCare
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: security@summitcare.com <security@summitcare.com>, Emma Liu <emma.liu@summitcare.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot question — what exactly do you keep by default?

Hi Julian / Emma — quick answers to each item below. Reproducing the key lines so you can paste them in the questionnaire.

1) Prompts with PHI/PII:
- Default: Yes, they fall under the "Customer request/input" bucket and the default 45-day window applies.
- Shorten retention: Customers can enable a "sensitive-data purge" flag at ingestion that triggers immediate purge after request processing (typically within 5–15 minutes). This will also exclude the request from telemetry sampling. We'll include instructions in the Drive doc.

2) Deletion evidence sample (we attached a tiny example):
- deletion_job_id: dj-20260511-9af3
- affected_record_ids: [req-987234, out-987234]
- requested_by: summitcare@procurement.summitcare.com
- completed_at: 2026-05-11T16:12:05Z
- note: snapshot backups scheduled for deletion in background job queue (non-blocking)

3) Embeddings:
- Embeddings are treated separately: by default embeddings used for semantic features are retained for 180 days (they power similarity indexes and search). If you don't use Redwood-managed embeddings, you can opt to host indexes in your environment or set an auto-prune policy.

If you'd like, Kimberly can convert this into a one-paragraph vendor-ready answer and we can supply the two attachments as evidence. Let me know and we'll send the final packet.

Regards,
Olga

--- Attachments referenced in thread ---
1) redwood-retention-matrix.pdf (pdf) — matrix with categories, default timelines, and opt-out flags
2) sample-erasure-log.txt (txt) — small anonymized deletion job evidence example
